thread:
dana-support: Customer on private VPC is seeing a sudden spike of 429s and a billing jump after a token rotation. They report ~6k 429s in 10m and higher billed tokens despite retries failing. attaching short logs below.

chris-enginfra: can you paste the ingress controller type + gateway config? is this through the customer-managed gateway or our proxy?

dana-support: they run customer-managed gateway (helm deploy of our gateway image) sitting behind k8s nginx-ingress. Gateway config in customer repo: `rate_limit: { enabled: true, mode: local, bucket: { refill_qps: 100, capacity: 200 } }` — they also set ingress annotation `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "100"` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "50"`

Alice Mendez: quick thought — if the gateway is local token-bucket + nginx RPS limits, double-limiting and mismatch windows can cause a tight retry storm. If tokens expire on auth rotation, clients might retry rapidly until hitting nginx limit -> lots of rejected requests counted at the gateway and potentially reissued then billed. :thinking_face:

ben-platform: do we have request_id traces for these requests? if they retried with different auth token they might have hit billing each time. also want to see `x-forwarded-for` vs client ip so rate limiter isn't applied per-pod instead of per-customer.

dana-support: attaching snippet of gateway logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z WARN auth: token expired for client=acct-123
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z INFO request: id=req-9a3 client=acct-123 retry=1 route=/v1/generate status=401
2026-03-10T14:02:13Z INFO request: id=req-9a4 client=acct-123 retry=2 route=/v1/generate status=200 tokens=421
2026-03-10T14:02:14Z ERROR rate_limit: token-bucket exhausted client=acct-123 route=/v1/generate
2026-03-10T14:02:15Z INFO request: id=req-9a6 client=acct-123 retry=3 status=429
```

chris-enginfra: looks like two things: 1) auth rotation caused an initial 401 -> client retried and got a success (we should check why retry succeeded after 401), 2) after some successes, rate limiter reported exhausted and 429s followed. Important: are nginx RPS limits applied per upstream IP (pods) or per client IP? If per-pod, bursts from many clients could be funneled to same pod and cause local exhaustion.

Alice Mendez: recommended quick checks:
- verify `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps` vs envoy/per-route descriptors; make sure limits are per-header `X-Customer-ID` not per source IP
- check gateway config `mode: local` -> if they have multiple pods, local token buckets are per-pod; recommend `mode: distributed` or a centralized quota service for consistent throttling
- confirm auth middleware order: auth should reject before rate-limit checks to avoid billing for unauthorized requests

ben-platform: also check retry policy on client side. If they use exponential backoff with jitter it's okay; tight loops will amplify bursts. If we see header `Retry-After` missing, clients may hammer. We should return `Retry-After` on 429s.

dana-support: customer confirms nginx was defaulting to `limit-rps` per IP. their k8s nodes are behind NAT so many client addresses mapped to same external IP -> per-IP limits were colliding.

quota-bot: Automated check: found 3 pods of gateway, each with `rate_limit.bucket.capacity=200` and ingress annotation RPS=50. Combined effective observed limit per logical customer was ~150 qps before nginx per-IP kicked in.

Alice Mendez: short mitigation steps to propose to customer (can be applied ASAP):
1) change nginx ingress annotation to use `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-by: "header"` and set header to `X-Customer-ID` (ensures per-customer throttling). Example: `kubectl annotate ingress my-ingress nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-by="header" nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-by-header="X-Customer-ID"`
2) switch gateway `rate_limit.mode` from `local` -> `distributed` (or increase per-pod capacity) while we investigate
3) ensure auth middleware runs before billing counters and return `Retry-After` on 429s.

chris-enginfra: sample nginx annotation (from docs):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: my-ingress
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-by: "header"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-by-header: "X-Customer-ID"
```

ben-platform: if customer is uncomfortable changing to distributed right away we can suggest an interim increase to `bucket.capacity` to absorb the burst: `capacity: 1000` and `refill_qps: 200` for 5-10m window, then scale down. But warn about cost.

dana-support: customer applied the header-based limit and bumped capacity to 800. after 8m they report 429s fell to <30 and billing spikes stopped. they also asked for a runbook to avoid in the future.

Alice Mendez: propose runbook entries:
- preflight on token rotations: emit a `400` with descriptive body if auth header malformed -> avoid retries.
- ensure `Retry-After` and `x-rate-limit-*` headers are present on 429 responses
- recommend traffic shaping at edge (CDN or LB) to smooth spikes into gateway pools
- monitoring: alert if 429 rate > 1% of total or if per-customer qps variance > 3x baseline

chris-enginfra: I'll open an internal PR to add the `Retry-After` header when gateway returns 429 and add a config flag to run auth before billing. tagging @ben-platform for cost implications.

ben-platform: ack. will estimate cost impact of temporary capacity increase and draft billing-friendly guidance.

dana-support: customer very happy with quick fix. marking thread for follow-up next week to push runbook and add docs snippet for onprem customers. :thumbsup:

Alice Mendez: nice work team. closing once PRs are merged. (reacted :tada:)
